summary: Players roll dice each turn and use them as workers of varying strength to develop their province, buy goods, and gain karma, racing to make their money and fame markers cross on two tracks running in opposite directions. It's a tight, puzzly euro where dice-as-workers creates constant tactical decisions about which action is worth which die.
praised: Elegant win-condition (fame and money tracks crossing)
criticised: Some luck in dice rolls, though mitigated by karma points
Rules have a few fiddly exceptions

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light racing
interaction.detail: Each player develops their own province board largely independently; the main touchpoint is racing for the same track positions and market goods, plus a shared game-end trigger. There is minimal direct conflict or blocking.

scoring.why: The game ends the instant a player's money marker and fame marker meet on their two opposed tracks, so reaching that intersection first is the entire win condition rather than a final tally.
scoring.how_you_win: You use workers and dice to build your province, gain goods, and earn karma, pushing your fame token and money token along two tracks that run in opposite directions; the first player whose tokens meet or cross wins immediately.
